subject: QH MAP: Technical evaluation milestone checklist & owners
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: QH MAP: Technical evaluation milestone checklist & owners

Hi Laura — thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Per our discussion, I captured a compact technical-eval milestone plan (attached) so we can lock responsibilities and the target close date for the MAP. Key points here and next steps below.

Summary (what we recommend as the "Technical Evaluation" MAP milestone):
- Objective: Validate model quality, latency and cost for the primary customer flows (claims intake + eligibility Q&A).
- Success criteria (pass/fail gating):
  * Quality: end-to-end accuracy/intent score >= 88% on seed test set; top-3 answer coverage >= 95% for routing tasks.
  * Latency: P50 <= 180ms; P95 <= 700ms for 1-2k token requests in our canary environment.
  * Unit economics: tokenized cost <= $0.015 / 1k effective tokens under realistic batching profiles.
- Shortlist: Redwood-v1-small (quantized), LlamaX-13B-q4, Mistral-7B-ptq (candidates for initial benchmark).

Proposed milestones & owners (high level):
1) Access & data handoff (owner: QuantumHealth: Laura / Alan) — secure test dataset + sample traffic capture (due: 2026-12-08)
2) Environment prep (owner: Redwood: Ben) — canary infra + KMS/VPC config, credentials (due: 2026-12-15)
3) Benchmark run #1 (owner: Redwood: Marissa + Ben) — baseline latency/cost with 3 model candidates (due: 2026-12-22)
4) Quality tuning & rerun (owner: Redwood + QH SMEs) — prompt engineering + quantization validation (due: 2027-01-05)
5) Readout & decision (owner: QuantumHealth + Redwood leadership) — recommend model + rollout plan (target MAP close: 2027-01-15)

Dependencies and risks:
- Need access to sample PII-scrubbed dataset and test traffic.
- Procurement lead time for dedicated VPC/SLA if QH opts for Dedicated (may push timeline).
- SOC2 evidence requests could add compliance gating.

Attachments: initial_map_draft.xlsx, benchmark_seed_prompts.md (seed prompts we agreed on).

Would you confirm owners and the first access date (Dec 8) so we can lock infra reservations? Happy to jump on a 30-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Dylan

3) Data: we'll provide a scrubbed 2k-row sample and one week of synthetic traffic. Alan (copied) will coordinate delivery.

I've attached our security questionnaire for redwood to review (security_qs.pdf).

If you can provide a short note on the load profile and cost assumptions by EOD tomorrow, we'll confirm Dec 8 handoff.

Best,

Subject: Re: QH MAP: Technical evaluation milestone checklist & owners

Laura — thanks for the quick read. A couple quick answers and the assumptions baked into our latency/cost targets (summary):

Load profile assumptions for the latency numbers:
- Canary environment: single-GPU worker with concurrent request handling tuned for 40 qps sustained (burst to 80 qps).
- Benchmark run: synthetic replay at 20 qps for latency profile collection; 95th-percentile measured over steady-state 5-min window.
- Batch behavior: continuous batching with target batch window 12-18ms (typical for low-latency small-batch workloads).

Cost assumptions for $0.015 / 1k tokens:
- Includes inference engine op-efficiency (quantized runtime), storage for KV cache and network egress estimates for hosted/dedicated scenario.
- Does NOT include one-time infra setup (procurement, dedicated VPC set up) or long-term reserved commit discounts. We can model those separately for procurement.

Preliminary model shortlist rationale:
- Redwood-v1-small (q8/q4 path): lowest latency and simplest to tune for the flows you described.
- LlamaX-13B-q4: higher quality on longer context items (eligibility paragraphs) but higher cost; use if Redwood-v1 fails quality gates.
- Mistral-7B-ptq: strong quality/cost tradeoff in our internal benchmarks — good middle ground.

I've uploaded a short benchmark plan doc to the Drive: redwood-benchmark-plan-v1.docx (link in the MAP). If that aligns I'll schedule the infra prep tasks and reserve canary slots for 12/14-12/22.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Owner map (detailed):

- VPN / KMS access & certs: QuantumHealth security + Redwood infra (Ben)
- Canary infra provisioning & model deployment: Redwood infra (Ben)

Dependencies we need from QH to hit the 2027-01-15 MAP close:

- Access to a sample of production traffic or synthetic capture with typical request sizes (due 2026-12-10).
- Procurement contact and expected lead times for Dedicated (if chosen) — please share contact by 12/06.

Compliance note: If QH requires Redwood to run in a Private (VPC) deployment for the eval, that adds ~2 weeks for infra and KMS onboarding. We'll keep Hosted canary as default to avoid that delay, unless you need Private for legal reasons.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Laura/Alan confirm dataset delivery date (Dec 8) — reply-all.
2) Ben to create canary infra ticket and list exact credentials we need (target: 12/03 EOD).
3) Marissa will draft the benchmark acceptance rubric and upload it to the Drive by 12/06.

If everyone is aligned I'll convert the Excel into a formal MAP milestone entry in HubSpot (HS-93427) and we can set a follow-up checkpoint meeting the week of 12/13.

-Marissa
